newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Repairs start on Tsumeb copper smelter.
newsitem.headline: Repairs start on Tsumeb copper smelter.

text.p: Gold Fields Namibia Ltd said on Wednesday repair work had started on the damaged smelter at its Tsumeb Corp Ltd (TCL) unit in northern Namibia.

"They are starting to proceed with the breaking down of the copper smelter so it can be rebuilt," said a spokesman by telephone from Namibia, adding the repair work would probably take six to eight weeks.
The smelter was extensively damaged when copper solidified after workers took control of the site at the start of a strike over pay.
The company has regained control of TCL but the four-week-old strike continues, halting production.

The spokesman said the company was still waiting for the Mineworkers' Union of Namibia to get back to mediators in the dispute. The union said last week it was seeking a postponement in the mediation until September 20 at the latest.
A Namibian court on Wednesday granted a final order upholding parts of an interim interdict restricting striking employees from interfering with mine equipment, the spokesman said.
A decision on two paragraphs from the interim interdict regarding the legality of the strike was postponed, pending oral evidence.

TCL mines and smelters have been shut down since August 23 when strikers took control of key areas. Since then 1,000 non-striking workers have returned to work, but output remains at a standstill with some 1,500 workers still out on strike.
The strike is costing TCL some 80 tonnes a day in lost copper production and a similar amount in lost lead.
The lead smelter appears undamaged, but will still take two to three weeks to restart.
TCL produced just under 30,000 tonnes of blister copper last year and 27,000 tonnes of lead. Most of the lead was produced from bought-in material while copper output was from TCL mines.
